analysis:
During a Lok Sabha debate on an adjournment motion on black money in December 2011, the Finance Minister said the government would bring out a White Paper on black money. The motion was defeated by voice vote and the government declined to disclose names of foreign account holders, citing treaty constraints.

The White Paper on Black Money was presented to Parliament on 16 May 2012. It discussed definitions, channels of generation and measures such as double-taxation agreements, but did not give a single official estimate of the quantum of black money; the Finance Minister noted in its foreword that quantification reports were still awaited.

The specific commitment — to publish a white paper — was fulfilled.
notes: The quote is a reported summary from The Hindu, not a verbatim transcript. No fixed deadline was announced with the promise, so deadline is null. The claim covers the promise to publish the paper, not the separate and unresolved question of recovering black money.
